subject: chemistry
title: Gibbs Galaxy: Free Energy and Feasibility
welcome_lead: Use ΔG = ΔH - TΔS to judge whether a reaction can proceed.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on Gibbs free energy and reaction feasibility.
final_note: You hold the master key to spontaneity.

concepts.def: Thermodynamic ability for reaction to occur.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Watch units: ΔH in kJ, ΔS in J/K. Convert: divide ΔS by 1000 or multiply ΔH by 1000 first.

If ΔH<0 and ΔS>0: always spontaneous. If ΔH>0 and ΔS<0: never. Other combinations depend on T.

Set ΔG = 0 -> T = ΔH/ΔS. Above (or below) this T, reaction becomes feasible depending on signs.

For CaCO3 decomposition (ΔH>0, ΔS>0), reaction is feasible only above T_min ~ 1100 K.

Feasible (ΔG<0) does not mean fast. A high activation energy can keep a reaction kinetically inert.

Example: diamond -> graphite has ΔG<0 but Ea is huge. Catalysts lower Ea without changing ΔG.
